subject.title: fix #95895: [Security]: GEMINI_API_KEY written as a plaintext literal in the generated systemd service unit

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrowed policy that makes selected Google/Gemini auth-profile env refs file-backed in generated systemd service environments while leaving other auth-profile env refs unchanged?
rationale: The patch is mechanically small and source-backed, but it changes how installed services receive provider credentials; CI can prove delivery mechanics, not the intended security and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Accept The Narrow File-Backed Policy
options.body: Merge this PR after current-head checks remain green if maintainers agree the existing EnvironmentFile contract is the right boundary for Google/Gemini auth-profile keys.

options.title: Request A Generic Auth-Profile Policy
options.body: Ask for a revised PR if the desired contract is to route all safe auth-profile env refs through a shared policy instead of a Google/Gemini allowlist.

options.title: Keep Auth-Profile Rendering Separate
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want the linked security issue limited to config SecretRefs and separate auth-profile work later.

recommendation.title: Accept The Narrow File-Backed Policy
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after current-head checks remain green if maintainers agree the existing EnvironmentFile contract is the right boundary for Google/Gemini auth-profile keys.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current-main config SecretRef repair for the same issue and have the clearest recent maintainer-side history on this service-env boundary.
